messages:
Maya (Finance): FYI invoice from TallinTech (TT-EE-007). They put 'reverse charge - EU B2B' and VAT ID EE10203040. Net EUR 6,750. But their email also says 'please gross-up 7% local withholding'  which sounds off for intra-EU B2B. Can AP process or need docs?
Priya (Accounts Payable): Hold payment for now. If it's reverse charge and billed to our EU entity, VAT is recipient-accountable. But gross-up request is unusual. Do we have our EU VAT number on file for the billed entity?
Jaan (Vendor Ops): Vendor confirms invoice to Redwood EMEA Ltd (Dublin). They attached only the invoice PDF. No Certificate of Tax Residence or explanation for the 7% ask.
Hanna (Legal): Two things: 1) For reverse charge we need the vendor invoice to state reverse charge and include both VAT numbers (vendor + recipient). 2) Any withholding request requires vendor to provide legal basis + CORT and ideally proof of prior practice. Gross-up is a contract change. Don't gross-up without signed amendment.
TaxBot: Auto-check: EE VAT format EE######## matches EE10203040. Reverse charge within EU B2B is standard if billed to an EU VAT-registered customer. EU member states generally don't impose additional withholding on intra-EU B2B services; 7% claim looks non-standard. Recommend vendor provide: Certificate of Tax Residence, citation of Estonian law/tax guidance they rely on, and a reissued invoice that shows reverse charge properly (include our Irish VAT IE9999999FH).
Maya (Finance): Action list: Jaan request CORT + reissued invoice referencing reverse charge + vendor explanation for 7% withholding and any statutory reference. Priya will block payment until docs provided. Hanna to review if they insist on gross-up.
Priya (Accounts Payable): Blocking payment in AP system now and flagging as "awaiting tax docs (EE)".
Jaan (Vendor Ops): Drafting vendor message (pasting):
```
Hi TallinTech,
Thanks for the invoice. To process we require: 1) Certificate of Tax Residence (CORT) or Estonian tax authority confirmation; 2) A reissued invoice that clearly states "reverse charge - recipient liable" and includes both your VAT EE10203040 and our billed entity VAT (Redwood EMEA Ltd VAT IE9999999FH); 3) If you require a 7% gross-up, provide the legal basis (statute or official guidance) and a worked example calculation and indicate whether this is standard practice for your clients; 4) confirmation of place of performance of services.
Please provide within 72 hours so we can avoid payment delays.
Thanks,
Jaan
```
Hanna (Legal): If they supply a statute, we'll review. If their counsel insists on a withholding, require a written amendment to the contract before any gross-up. If they provide CORT showing Estonian residence and a clear tax remittance receipt tied to this invoice, we can consider post-payment substantiation, but prefer the docs first.
TaxBot: Note: If services were actually performed outside Estonia (e.g., remote work from non-EE jurisdiction), Estonian withholding likely doesn't apply. Ask vendor to state location of performance on the invoice.
Maya (Finance): Thanks. Please update thread when vendor replies. :eyes:
